owner_source.verbatim: said too many requests so i guess 20s is a good min, let's change the 60s min to 20s in MC but just make sure each worker is queuing them globally

normalized_outcome: Mission Control uses a 20-second configured minimum between provider send boundaries while preserving one shared, durable, global queue/admission/lease authority for all worker and relay sends. Workers must not bypass the Mission Control queue, create per-worker send authority, or race independently.

required_outcomes.observable: The central Mission Control submission authority default and accepted lower bound are 20000 ms, and diagnostics evaluate violations against the configured minimum plus the 20-second policy floor.
Relay configuration and defense-in-depth pacing defaults align with the same 20000 ms configured minimum and reject values below 20000 ms for the central authority path.
Tests prove requests from workers/hosts still serialize through the single durable FIFO queue and active lease before any send boundary.

non_satisfying_proxies: changing only a host-local relay pacer
changing only documentation without the central authority lower bound
a direct browser/send test that bypasses Mission Control
per-worker timers or locks replacing the global Mission Control queue
a 20-second UI label while the BFF/daemon still rejects values below 60000 ms
green tests that do not cover the global queue/admission gate
production_boundary: Changing the live VPS Mission Control pacing configuration or deploying this candidate requires exact hosted/local verification and a live no-send authority/status check; direct provider-send stress testing is not required by this requirement.
next_direct_evidence: Run focused Mission Control and relay scheduler/config tests, then deploy the exact verified candidate only if crossing the live configuration boundary is authorized by this owner request and live no-send status confirms queue depth, active lease, configured minimum, and zero ambiguity.
